item.title: Research (Verify): Which quick fact-checking moves fit how we label known issues as reported or confirmed?
item.description: SIFT's last two moves are to find better coverage of a claim and trace it to its original context. Our sourcing rules already trace updates to the changelog, but each of the 4 reported issues rests on one source. Idea for standup: when open issues are rechecked, Verify looks for one more independent report and notes it, with no label change on its own.

item.title: Research (Scout): Why does the official changelog feed fail from the box, and can the daily run read it directly again?
item.description: The feed isn't down. With curl's default user agent the box gets a 403; with a browser user agent it gets a 200 RSS file listing 0.78.1 first, matching updates.json. Yesterday's 'Cloudflare block' came from the default agent. Pitch: the daily run fetches the feed with a named user agent and says which way it read the changelog.

item.title: Research (Comms): Does our llms.txt still match the current llms.txt proposal, now that it has a v2?
item.description: Our file has the shape v2 asks for: an H1, a summary blockquote, notes, H2 link lists and an Optional section. v2 adds two things we don't do: a rel=describedby link from pages to llms.txt, and markdown copies of pages. Pitch: the describedby link in the shared head, one line. Markdown copies stay out; they'd double the site.
